question:
Consider the matrix $A=\begin{bmatrix}a & 1 & 1\\1 & a & 1\\1 & 1 & a\end{bmatrix}$.

(a) Evaluate $|A|$ as a polynomial in $a$.

(b) Factorise the polynomial obtained.

(c) Determine all real values of $a$ for which $|A|=0$, and verify each value by substitution in the factorised form.
explanation:
(a)
Expanding along the first row,
$$|A|=a\begin{vmatrix}a & 1\\1 & a\end{vmatrix}-\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1\\1 & a\end{vmatrix}+\begin{vmatrix}1 & a\\1 & 1\end{vmatrix}$$
$$|A|=a(a^2-1)-(a-1)+(1-a)$$
$$|A|=a^3-a-a+1+1-a$$
$$|A|=a^3-3a+2$$

(b)
Since $a=1$ is a zero, $(a-1)$ is a factor. Dividing and factorising further gives
$$a^3-3a+2=(a-1)(a^2+a-2)$$
$$a^3-3a+2=(a-1)^2(a+2)$$

(c)
For $|A|=0$,
$$(a-1)^2(a+2)=0$$
Therefore,
$$a=1\quad\text{or}\quad a=-2$$
For $a=1$,
$$|A|=(1-1)^2(1+2)=0$$
For $a=-2$,
$$|A|=(-2-1)^2(-2+2)=0$$
Hence, the required real values are $a=1$ and $a=-2$.
